text: Blueprint set security headers app-wide instead of on its own routes

Fixed in cb72af1 (server-only).

The app-wide after_request hook now self-limits to routes this extension owns
rather than switching to @bp.after_request as the report suggested — that would
have silently dropped CSP/X-Frame-Options/no-referrer from the invite landing
page and SPA, which are registered at the site root outside url_prefix (Spec §5)
and so have request.blueprint == None. Ownership = our blueprint name(s) in
app.extensions[EXTENSION_KEY], OR request.endpoint in a per-app set of the
site-root endpoints we actually registered (only added when the route really got
registered — APK/web bundle can be absent).

Report's fix #2 (setdefault) was already implemented, so no header was ever
overwritten; the remaining bug was ADDING headers to responses we don't own.
Chose not to add the suggested global_headers opt-in flag: scoping to our own
routes is behavior-identical in the standalone wheel (we own the whole app) and
strictly safer when co-mounted, so there's no use case for the app-wide variant.

Regression tests (tests/test_hardening.py): our headers reach none of a
co-mounted foreign blueprint's HTML/POST responses nor an unrelated plain host
route, and the flip side — our own API still gets headers when co-mounted.

Full server suite 261 passed. Web/Android untouched. NOT released — batched for
the next release with T-103/T-104/T-105.
